title: Welcome to the Real World: How You Live in Your Own Simulation of Reality — and How We Can Still Share a World. A Theory of Persistence, Emergence, Learning, and Correctable Intelligence
description: Evolution by Emergence is an open research corpus and machine-auditable candidate architecture for resource-constrained cumulative evolution. Version v23.0 is a major release: the core now opens with what a functional world model is, the question its title asks. A world model is any representation that lets a holder infer what it does not observe, what may happen and what would happen if it acted. A functional world model is held, for a stated scope and use, with the aim of fitting how things are; it is tested against evidence whose outcomes are not fixed by the claims tested; it aims to be as sharp as the evidence supports, subject to calibration where calibration can be assessed; and it is correctable, in its beliefs, its background assumptions and its range of possibilities. In a collective, its quality depends both on what contributors pass on and on how contributions are combined. CORE.md follows this opening with one model of learning, read as a network, in eight steps, and formalization/ebe-core/EbECore.lean now audits 96 machine-checked results, five of them from a new core-Lean module, WorldModel, on evidential fit, inconsistency, revision by retracting false evidence, and veto versus weighted pooling. The definition note was shaped by three independent reviews by AI readers of other model families, kept as received with a response to each. Retained from earlier releases: the integrity of world models and neurorights, the building-the-future essay, identity as a learned path, TamedCapture, duties to the quality of a relationship, a shared identity as learners, and a separate section on transparent pricing with its own 76-result core-Lean package. DIALOGUE.md records how the author and an AI assistant build the model together, now in 34 entries. The release title uses ‘simulation of reality’ to mean the internal model through which a system experiences and acts in the world, not a claim that reality itself is simulated. Formal verification establishes implications under explicit premises; empirical, causal, political and normative interpretations remain open.
